Tuning of an INLAvaan fit

Source: R/inlavaan-control.R
inlavaan_control.Rd

Builds the control list of inlavaan(), acfa(), asem() and agrowth(): the limits of the search for the posterior mode, of the VB correction and of the skew-normal scans, and three settings for checks and development. The defaults suit most fits, so most users never need it. A plain list with some of these names works too, and is checked by the same rules: control = list(n_grid = 31) is the same as control = inlavaan_control(n_grid = 31).

Usage

inlavaan_control(
  mode_maxit = 5000L,
  mode_maxeval = 5000L,
  mode_tol = 1e-10,
  vb_maxit = 25L,
  vb_tol = 0.001,
  vb_budget = 2,
  n_grid = 21L,
  log_threshold = -6,
  nlminb = list(),
  hessian = c("central", "forward"),
  debug = FALSE,
  add_priors = TRUE
)

Arguments

mode_maxit, mode_maxeval

The largest number of iterations, and of evaluations of the log-posterior, of the search for the posterior mode by stats::nlminb() (its iter.max and eval.max). When the search stops short of the mode, it starts once more from where it stopped, with each parameter scaled by its curvature and the same limits.

mode_tol

The relative tolerance of the search for the posterior mode (the rel.tol of stats::nlminb()).

vb_maxit, vb_tol

The largest number of iterations, and the tolerance in posterior SDs, of the fixed-point iteration of the VB correction. They act with vb_correction = "full", and on the solve that follows a failed check of the default one-step correction. A first step below vb_tol in every parameter is not checked.

vb_budget

The cap on the solve that follows a failed check of the default one-step correction. The solve and the two passes of the check together take at most vb_budget times the evaluations of the log-posterior, of its gradient and of the Hessian that the search for the posterior mode and the Hessian made, in passes of the rule of 2m + 1 gradients each, for m parameters. Default 2. 1 is the cap of earlier development versions, Inf lifts the cap, so that the solve stops only at vb_tol or after vb_maxit iterations, and 0 leaves a flagged fit at its mode. A single number of at least 0. A fit that passes the check does not depend on it. The cap scales with the cost of the search for the mode, so a search from a good start, as in a warm-started update(), leaves less room for the solve.

n_grid

The number of points of the scan of each skew-normal marginal, over 4 posterior SDs on each side of the mode. At least 7. It replaces the deprecated argument sn_fit_ngrid of inlavaan().

log_threshold

Points of the scan whose log-posterior falls more than this below the maximum are left out of the skew-normal fit. The five highest points are always kept. A single negative number. It replaces the deprecated argument sn_fit_logthresh of inlavaan().

nlminb

A named list of other controls of stats::nlminb() for the search for the posterior mode, such as trace = 1, which prints its iterations, or abs.tol. Its iter.max, eval.max and rel.tol stand in for mode_maxit, mode_maxeval and mode_tol, which must then not be set too. It does not reach the optimiser that the VB correction falls back to.

hessian

How the Hessian at the posterior mode is differenced from the analytic gradient. "central" (default) costs two gradient evaluations per parameter. "forward" costs about half as much but is less accurate, and suits models with many parameters and large samples. It replaces the deprecated argument hessian_method of inlavaan().

debug

Logical. With TRUE, the fit returns its internal list (see get_inlavaan_internal()) instead of an INLAvaan object, for development. Default FALSE. It replaces the deprecated argument debug of inlavaan().

add_priors

Logical. With FALSE, the log-posterior leaves out the priors, so that the posterior mode is the maximum likelihood estimate. Only the mode is meaningful then. Default TRUE. It replaces the deprecated argument add_priors of inlavaan().

Value

A list of the entries that were set, checked, for the control argument of inlavaan(). An entry left out takes its default. An iter.max, eval.max or rel.tol given in nlminb is returned as mode_maxit, mode_maxeval or mode_tol.

Details

Give each setting in one place only: an entry and the deprecated argument of inlavaan() that it replaces (for example n_grid and sn_fit_ngrid) cannot both be set, and neither can an entry and its twin in nlminb.

Up to INLAvaan 0.3.5, control was a list of controls of stats::nlminb(), such as control = list(iter.max = 2000). These names still work in control, with a deprecation warning, and stop from INLAvaan 0.5.0: iter.max, eval.max and rel.tol set mode_maxit, mode_maxeval and mode_tol, and the others go to nlminb.

See also

inlavaan(), stats::nlminb()

Examples

# A finer scan of each skew-normal marginal
inlavaan_control(n_grid = 31)
#> $n_grid
#> [1] 31
#> 

# Print the iterations of the search for the posterior mode
inlavaan_control(nlminb = list(trace = 1))
#> $nlminb
#> $nlminb$trace
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> 

# An iter.max in nlminb stands in for mode_maxit
inlavaan_control(nlminb = list(iter.max = 200))
#> $mode_maxit
#> [1] 200
#> 
#> $nlminb
#> list()
#> 

# \donttest{
utils::data("HolzingerSwineford1939", package = "lavaan")
fit <- acfa(
  "visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3",
  HolzingerSwineford1939,
  test = "none",
  control = inlavaan_control(n_grid = 31)
)
#> ✔ Found the posterior mode in 25 iterations [24ms]
#> ✔ VB mean correction, max shift 0.47σ [15ms]
#> ✔ Fitted 6 skew-normal marginals [78ms]
#> ⠙ Drawing posterior samples.
#> ✔ Draw 1000 posterior samples. [54ms]
#> 

# The same with a plain list
fit <- acfa(
  "visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3",
  HolzingerSwineford1939,
  test = "none",
  control = list(n_grid = 31)
)
#> ✔ Found the posterior mode in 25 iterations [25ms]
#> ✔ VB mean correction, max shift 0.47σ [14ms]
#> ✔ Fitted 6 skew-normal marginals [77ms]
#> ⠙ Drawing posterior samples.
#> ✔ Draw 1000 posterior samples. [64ms]
#> 
# }
